title: The nutritional value of invertebrate aquatic foods.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the Zenodo zip (3.1 MB, CC-BY-4.0). Opened data final/20250902_raw_spspecific_invertdata.csv: 18,052 rows x 173 columns in long format (one row per sample x nutrient), 474 species, 192 studies, 42 nutrients, units column (mg/mcg/g), 261 missing values, 125 'tr' (trace) flags, 543 zeros. Largest single nutrient (iron) has 1,038 rows from 334 species and 104 studies. sample_year filled on 4,763 rows. 70% of rows come from food composition tables. All .rds model outputs and predictions are Git LFS pointer stubs (133 bytes), not data. AllSLBSpecies_Traits.csv: 71,591 species x 20 trait columns. AllSLBSpecies_EdibleInverts.csv fails to parse as UTF-8 (needs latin-1).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 13,888 samples / 465 species count, the Bayesian hierarchical model (brms) design, the leave-one-out and k-fold cross-validation comparisons in Supplementary Tables 5-6 (supplement not retrievable: Europe PMC endpoint timed out), and the 50,807-species prediction set.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked in files: Zenodo zip downloads openly, CC-BY-4.0; but model outputs and predictions are Git LFS stubs, so only the raw tables are usable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in files: measured nutrient concentration is the 'value' column with 'nutrient' and 'nutrient_units' columns; would need pivoting per nutrient, not construction.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked in files: taxonomy (phylum to genus) and SeaLifeBase traits (Lmax maximum length, trophic level, depth, temperature regime, habitat flags) sit in the same table, 80-94% filled.

a4_units_stated.note: Checked in files: units column present (mg, mcg, g per 100 g); one oddity, lysine listed in mcg while other amino acids are mg, so units need a sanity check.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked in files: 18,052 rows pooled, but each nutrient is a separate label and the largest (iron) has only 1,038 rows from 334 species; the real independent unit is the species (474 total), well under the ~1,500-row bar.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Checked in files: tiny tabular working set.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Checked in files: 18,052 sample-nutrient rows and 474 species vs paper's 13,888 samples and 465 species; plausibly explained by long format and name versions, not verified exactly.

a8_label_provenance.note: Checked in files: values are laboratory measurements compiled from peer-reviewed papers (5,176 rows) and food composition tables (12,599 rows), not model output.

existing_models.name: This paper's Bayesian hierarchical models (brms, taxonomy plus traits)
existing_models.score_and_split: Compared to taxonomy-only and intercept-only models by leave-one-out and k-fold cross-validation (Supplementary Tables 5-6, not retrieved); fitted model files are Git LFS stubs in the Zenodo record.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Within- and between-species variation over space and time; data-poor species without trait data collapse to dominant patterns.

existing_models.name: Hicks et al. 2019 / Vaitla et al. 2018 fish nutrient models (NutrientFishbase, Bayesian phylogeny plus traits)
existing_models.score_and_split: Fish only, not invertebrates; scores not retrieved.

backbone.name: None fits; inputs are taxonomy and ecological traits, not sequences or molecules

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which unmeasured edible invertebrates are likely nutrient-dense, already done by the paper itself.

controls.positive_control: Molluscs higher in B12 and iron than crustaceans (paper's finding).
controls.external_validation: Partial sample_year column (4,763 rows) for a temporal split; none independent.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts the per-100 g concentration of one nutrient for an invertebrate species from its taxonomy and SeaLifeBase traits, among ~330 mostly commercially eaten mollusc and crustacean species measured in food composition tables.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an aquatic invertebrate species' family tree position and ecological traits to predict how much of each nutrient its edible tissue contains.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-sample nutrient measurements with species taxonomy, body part, cooking method and traits; 18,052 sample-nutrient rows but only 474 species, at most 1,038 rows per nutrient.
plain_idea.predict: Concentration of a nutrient (for example iron in mg per 100 g), measured in laboratories and compiled from papers and national food composition tables.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Nutrition and fisheries policy groups could prioritise unmeasured species, but the paper's own Bayesian model already does this for 50,807 species.

ml_idea: Multi-output regression of 30 nutrients from taxonomy plus traits with a leave-genus-out split, compared against the authors' Bayesian hierarchical model. Too few independent species per nutrient, no pretrained backbone, and the task is already done by the paper.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 19 MB CSV size; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count distinct species per nutrient after dropping food-composition-table duplicates; iron already tops out at 334 species.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 in disguise: the independent unit is the species (474 total, at most 334 for any one nutrient, 1,038 rows max per nutrient), no pretrained backbone fits taxonomy-plus-trait inputs, and the paper already fits and cross-validates a predictive model for exactly this task.
